text: Come on, honey. Deedee hasn't missed a dance floor in fifty years. One, two, three.

Oh my!

Hugs for everyone. There. All better.

Hugs for everyone, just because. To the moon and back.

To the moon and BACK.

So they are. Not one word to Boppy.

Who told you that.
Tata is on thin ice.
Hand me my glasses. I want to look at him properly. Where ARE my glasses.

Somebody read me that plaque. My glasses are in my other purse.
Oh. So I am. Well then.
I couldn't FIND them, honey.
None for me, Justin. Store-bought gives me gas.
Fine. One slice. For the girl who said it.

You're wearing the tie.

Look at you. Making a friend.

Fifty-two years, and he still asks. Every time.
Admitted by moonlight. Oh, I have goosebumps. Tommy, feel my arm.
Up, everybody. Deedee is a nurse.
Then sway with your mother.
Tommy. Dance with your mother.

Admit three, Tommy. You. Me. And Boppy.

Tommy, whatever her shiny side shows bounces right back. Use something else. And honey, nobody has asked her to dance since 1971. Three times.

A layover! Where? Never mind. Take a sweater. Take two. Take the crisp.
